data.narrative:
Mujin is a Series C robotics and manufacturing automation company that has raised $85M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 9 private companies and 1 public comparable, all operating in robotics and manufacturing at Series B through Series D stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $85M raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, yielding $144M. Peer-median analysis examines 7 same-sector comparables spanning Series B and D stages—including Exotec ($2.0B Series D), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B Series B), and Hadrian ($1.6B Series D)—producing a median valuation of $1.6B with a range of $1.0B to $2.0B.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $123M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $897M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around (1) Mujin's market positioning relative to the peer set, which spans substantial stage variance; (2) revenue traction and path to profitability; and (3) whether Series C advancement warrants compression toward the $144M stage-based floor or alignment with the higher $1.6B peer median. Narrowing this range would require clarity on current-period revenue, customer concentration, and burn dynamics relative to peer benchmarks.
